Where forcing can help, the result offers **Force delete**, which discards the listed work and ends the agent sessions running there.

### Update worktrees

To bring several worktrees and local branches up to date with their base branch at once:

1. On the Worktrees and branches sub-page, select the worktrees and branches.
2. Click **Update**. The **Update worktrees** dialog opens. Nothing changes until you confirm.
3. Under **How to update**, keep **Default** to use each repository's own setting (see [Edit a repository](#edit-a-repository)), or choose **Rebase** or **Merge** for this update.
4. Under **Push after update**, keep **Default**, or choose **Don't push**, **Push**, or **Push + Publish**. **Push** pushes only branches that already have a remote branch; **Push + Publish** also publishes the ones that do not.
5. Review the plan. Each row says how the branch will update and where it will be pushed, or **Skipped** with the reason, such as uncommitted changes or a conflict.
6. Click **Update**.

A branch with no worktree is updated in place; it is skipped if a worktree holds it or the main checkout has uncommitted changes. If Kepler prepared an update but could not apply it automatically, Kepler keeps it for you to review instead of discarding it.

When the update finishes, you can undo one row with **Roll back**, or every row with **Roll back all**. If you did not push during the update, **Push** and **Push all** push the updated branches that have an upstream. Kepler does not push a branch that moved since the update. The finished report stays in every window until you click **Dismiss**.

## Projects

Use **Projects** to group repositories that belong together under one name, such as a frontend and a backend you change together. A project's repositories act as a unit. The section has these controls:

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| A row | Opens the project's page |
| **New project** | Opens a page where you name a project and pick its repositories. **Add from folder** adds a repository without leaving the page |

To create the project, give it a name and click **Create**. After that, its page has no **Save** button: its name and each repository you tick or untick save as you change them. A folder's page saves its name and description the same way.

To delete a project, click **Delete project** on its page. Its repositories stay in your repository list.

***

# Integration Settings
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/settings-integrations/
product: Kepler
feature: Settings
content_type: reference
audience: developer
plan_required: all
status: GA
last_verified: 2026-11

Use **Settings → Integrations** to connect the issue trackers and Git hosts you start tasks from, and to choose what each one brings in.

## Issues and pull requests

Connect your issue and pull request providers to see their issues and pull requests in the **New task** composer and in [the Kepler interface](/kepler/kepler-interface). Kepler lists every supported provider, with the connected ones first: Azure DevOps, Azure DevOps Server, Bitbucket, Bitbucket Data Center, GitHub, GitHub Enterprise, GitLab, GitLab Self-Hosted, Jira, Jira Server / Data Center, Linear, Trello, and Asana.

Each provider row shows these controls and states:

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Connect** | Connects a provider you have not connected |
| **Connected** | Marks a working connection |
| **Reconnect** | Refreshes a token on a row marked **Sign-in expired** |
| **Cannot connect to server** | The server did not answer; the integration stays connected and the state clears on its own |
| **Unexpected response** | Kepler could not read the provider's answer, so some items may be missing; reconnecting does not fix it |
| **Disconnect** | Disconnects the account from every GitKraken product that uses it; other accounts stay connected |
| **Refresh** | Checks every provider's connection again, from the section header |

If a row shows **Cannot connect to server**, check that the server is reachable from your network or VPN. If **Unexpected response** stays, check for a proxy or gateway between Kepler and the provider.

Providers connect through your GitKraken account, so you sign in to GitKraken before you can manage them.

### Self-hosted providers

A self-hosted provider, such as GitHub Enterprise, Azure DevOps Server, Bitbucket Data Center, or Jira Server / Data Center, connects with a personal access token. Click **Connect**, enter the **Server URL** and **Personal access token**, then click **Save connection**. Kepler checks the token against your server and adds the connection to your GitKraken account. Until it finishes, the row shows **Cloud sync pending**.

To keep the token off your GitKraken account, tick **Keep PAT on this device only** before you save. The server URL and token then stay on this device, in its secure storage such as the system keychain, and the connection is not available on your other devices or in other GitKraken products.

A connected self-hosted provider lists each server on its own row. Each server keeps its own repositories and issues:

- To connect another server, click **Add connection** on the provider's row.
- To renew an expired or rejected token, click **Replace PAT** on that server's row.
- To move a token between your GitKraken account and this device, open the server row's storage chip (**GitKraken account** or **This device only**) and choose **Keep PAT on this device only** or **Store PAT in GitKraken account**. Kepler asks you to confirm first.
- To make a server the provider's default connection, click **Set as primary**.

### Choose what's visible

To hide organizations, repositories, or tracker projects you do not want in Kepler, click **Choose what's visible…** under the provider's row, then untick the items to hide. Every connected provider except Trello and Asana has it. A connection kept on this device only does not. Hidden items leave the dashboard, the launcher, and pickers, and tasks and branches already linked to them keep working. The choice is saved on your GitKraken account.

### Accounts and organizations

When a provider has more than 1 account, an **Accounts** block lists them. **Set as primary** chooses which account Kepler acts as, and **Read from this account** chooses which account Kepler reads issues and pull requests from. These can be different accounts, but agents' GitKraken MCP server always acts as the primary account. A self-hosted connection kept on this device only cannot be set as primary. See [MCP servers](/kepler/settings-agent-tools#mcp-servers).

When an organization refuses a working connection, because it blocks third-party OAuth apps or has not approved GitKraken, the row names the organization and says that its items are not shown. The row links to a fix, such as **Request access on GitHub**.

For per-provider setup, see [Issue Tracker Integrations](/kepler/issue-tracker-integrations) and [Pull Request Integrations](/kepler/pull-request-integrations).

## Your terminal

To follow agent sessions you start in your own terminal, use **Show them in Kepler** in **Settings → General → Sessions outside Kepler**. It is on by default. See [Sessions outside Kepler](/kepler/settings-app#sessions-outside-kepler).

***

---

---
# Action Settings
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/settings-actions/
product: Kepler
feature: Settings
content_type: reference
audience: developer
plan_required: all
status: GA
last_verified: 2026-11

Use **Settings → Actions** to save the prompts you use often and run them on a task, issue, or pull request without typing them again. An **Action** is an editable named prompt. The page has these sections:

| Section | What it holds |
|---|---|
| **Suggested Actions** | The Action that the button on each kind of item suggests: **Tasks**, **Issues**, **Pull requests I authored**, and **Pull requests from others** |
| **All Actions** | The built-in Actions under **Built in** and yours under **Custom**, each with what it does and where it is available |

Under **Suggested Actions**:

- Set a picker to **None** to leave only the menu on that kind of item.
- **Suggest automatically** switches a new task's button to the suggested Action when you link an issue or pull request to it. Turn it off to keep **Start**.

Under **All Actions**, click a row to edit it, use **Restore default** on a row you have edited, or use **Delete** on a custom row. To delete an Action that an [automation](/kepler/kepler-automations) runs, delete the automation first.

An Action can run with one of your [agent presets](/kepler/settings-agents#agent-presets), and the preset picks the agent. If the Action's preset no longer exists, its row shows **Preset unavailable for this agent** and the Action runs without it. To fix it, choose another preset in the Action's editor.

To create an Action, click **New Action** in the **All Actions** section header. **Restore all defaults**, beside it, discards every edit. An Action you create or edit opens as a sub-page.

Kepler has 4 built-in Actions, and each one is the default suggested Action for one kind of item:

- **Tasks** default to **Implement**.
- **Issues** default to **Plan**.
- Pull requests you authored default to **Address Feedback**.
- Pull requests from others default to **Review**.

For what the built-in Actions ask an agent to do, how the editor's **Title**, **Prompt**, **Available on**, and **Agent** fields behave, and how an Action picks the agent it runs on, see [Actions](/kepler/actions).

***

---

---
# Agent Tool Settings
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/settings-agent-tools/
product: Kepler
feature: Settings
content_type: reference
audience: developer
plan_required: all
status: GA
last_verified: 2026-11

Use **Settings → Agent tools** to manage the tools your agents can use beyond the ones they come with: [MCP servers](#mcp-servers) and Kepler's [built-in tools](#built-in-tools).

## MCP servers

Use **MCP servers** to give your agents extra tools, for example your issue tracker. The servers here are each agent's own defaults, and every repository inherits them.

To see the servers an agent loads, pick the agent with **Agent**. If that agent has more than 1 account, pick an account too. Kepler lists only the agents that expose their MCP servers to Kepler. In the list:

- Click a server to open its own page. There you can turn the server or a single tool off, sign in to a server that needs it, use **Also add to…** to copy the server to another agent, and **Remove server**.
- Click **Add server** in the section header to add one.

A server or tool you turn off here is off in every repository, unless a repository turns it back on for itself. A repository's own **MCP servers** section is on its [Edit repo](/kepler/settings-repositories#edit-a-repository) page. For some agents, you can also switch a server on or off for one session from the composer. See [MCP Servers](/kepler/mcp-servers).

Below the list, one more setting applies across every agent:

| Setting | What it controls | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Keep the GitKraken MCP server installed in every agent** | *Gives every command-line agent Git tools and your issues and pull requests through GitKraken. Turn off to manage it yourself.* | On |

Every session Kepler starts also gets Kepler's own workspace tools, which are always on and have no setting. With them, an agent can work with your tasks and their notes, links, files, and worktrees, and with sessions, approvals, and [themes](/kepler/settings-app#theme). With [Built-in tools](#built-in-tools) on, it can also rebase, merge, and compose commits. An agent can name a repository by one of its [aliases](/kepler/settings-repositories#edit-a-repository). For the full list of tools, see [Tasks and Resources](/kepler/tasks-and-resources).

In both Chat and Terminal, workspace tools run without the agent's own permission prompt. Instead, an action that needs your approval, such as deleting a worktree or changing another task, waits for you on an approval card. See [Approval Settings](/kepler/settings-approvals).

## Built-in tools

Use **Built-in tools** to let your agents call Kepler's own tools for rebasing, merging, and cleaning up commits:

| Setting | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **AI Sync** | *Lets agents rebase or merge your branch and resolve conflicts for you. Every change can be undone.* | Off |
| **AI Compose** | *Lets agents turn messy changes into clean, focused commits. Every change can be undone.* | Off |

A change applies to new agent sessions. Sessions already running keep the tools they started with.

***

---

---
# Approval Settings
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/settings-approvals/
product: Kepler
feature: Settings
content_type: reference
audience: developer
plan_required: all
status: GA
last_verified: 2026-11

Use **Settings → Approvals** to manage the rules that approve your agents' actions for you. Some actions your agents take wait for your approval, and an action that no rule covers still asks.

When an agent uses Kepler's workspace tools to do something that needs your approval, such as deleting a worktree, sending a prompt to another session, or rewriting a branch, Kepler pins an approval card above that session's message box. To create a rule for that kind of action, choose **Always approve** from the card's **Approve** menu. For an action that can lose work, such as deleting a worktree, Kepler names what is at risk and asks you to confirm first.

Some actions always ask, so their menu has no **Always approve**. For example:

- Adopting a task into another agent's work
- Adding a Run command to a repository, or replacing one
- Deleting a GitHub issue, which cannot be undone
- A setting change that Ask Kepler asks to make
- Starting a session in a more permissive mode

See [Agent Sessions](/kepler/agent-sessions#approval-requests).

## Always approved

**Always approved** lists each rule you create this way, with when and where you added it and how often it has run. **Remove** deletes the rule, so that kind of action asks again.

***

---

---
# App Settings
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/settings-app/
product: Kepler
feature: Settings
content_type: reference
audience: developer
plan_required: all
status: GA
last_verified: 2026-11

Use these Settings pages to change how Kepler itself looks and behaves:

- [General](#general): language, the default editor, sessions started outside Kepler, and windows
- [Appearance](#appearance): your theme for light and dark, the Dashboard's views, the code font, the diff layout, and Kep's seasonal touches
- [Chat and terminal](#chat-and-terminal): the chat's send key, width, and scrolling; the terminal's font, message box, and links; and whether the floating Ask Kepler panel hides on its own
- [Notifications](#notifications): which agent events notify you, on the desktop, in Kepler, and on your phone
- [Voice](#voice): a check of your microphone and speaker, dictation with its models and vocabulary, and read aloud
- [Keyboard shortcuts](#keyboard-shortcuts): look up and change Kepler's keyboard shortcuts

***

## General

Use **General** to choose Kepler's language, which editor opens your files, whether Kepler lists agent sessions you start outside it, and how its windows open.

### Language

**Language** has 1 setting:

| Setting | What it controls | Default | Options |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Language** | The display language for Kepler's interface | English | English, Español |

The language also applies to Kepler's native dialogs.

### Default editor

**Default editor** has 1 setting:

| Setting | What it controls | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Open files and folders in** | The app that **Open in** and **Ctrl/⌘ + Shift**-click on a file link use. The options are **Last used app**, each editor Kepler finds on this machine, and your system's default app | Last used app |

With your system's default app, files open without line numbers, and folders open in Finder, Explorer, or your file manager. If Kepler cannot open any editor from the window you are in, the setting says so.

### Sessions outside Kepler

To follow agent sessions you start in your own terminal, use this setting:

| Setting | What it controls | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Show them in Kepler** | Lists the agent sessions you run without Kepler, such as Claude Code or Codex in your own terminal, so you can read them or continue them in a task | On |

The setting covers every agent Kepler can follow this way. See [Agent Sessions](/kepler/agent-sessions#sessions-started-outside-kepler).

If a running agent session stops reporting to Kepler, every window shows *Agent sessions aren't reporting to Kepler*, with a **Repair** button. **Repair** reinstalls the reporting configuration. Restart any session that still does not report. For another computer's sessions, repair from that computer.

### Windows

These settings set how windows and folder dialogs work on this machine:

| Setting | What it controls | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Restore windows on launch** | *Reopens the windows you had open, with their size, page and connection. Turn off to start with one window.* | On |
| **Always use Kepler's folder picker** | Local windows open your system's folder dialog, and windows connected to another machine use Kepler's own folder picker, which can browse that machine. Turn this on to use Kepler's picker in every window | Off |

A change to **Restore windows on launch** takes effect the next time you start Kepler.

***

## Keep agents running

**Keep agents running** is a section of **Settings → Agents**: see [Keep agents running](/kepler/settings-agents#keep-agents-running).

### Idle agents

**Idle agents** is a section of **Settings → Agents**: see [Idle agents](/kepler/settings-agents#idle-agents).

***

## Appearance

Use **Appearance** to choose light or dark and a theme, and to set up the Dashboard's views, code text, diffs, and Kep. Kepler saves these settings on this machine.

### Theme

The **Theme** section has 2 parts: **Appearance**, which picks whether Kepler looks light or dark, and **Theme**, which picks the colors for each. Themes color the whole app, including code views, diffs, syntax, chat code blocks, and terminals.

**Appearance** has 3 options:

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| **System** | *Follows your system.* Kepler uses your dark theme when your OS is dark and your light theme when it's light, and switches when the OS does. **The default** |
| **Light** | *Always uses a light theme* |
| **Dark** | *Always uses a dark theme* |

Under **Theme**, each theme is a tile. The **Kepler** group holds the built-in themes:

- **Kepler**, which has a dark and a light version. It's the theme a fresh install uses for both.
- **Midnight**, a near-black theme that has only a dark version.

How you pick a tile depends on **Appearance**:

- On **System**, each tile has a moon and a sun. Click the moon to use the theme when your system is dark, or the sun to use it when your system is light. Click the tile itself to use it for both.
- On **Light** or **Dark**, click a tile to use it for that appearance.

The tile in use reads **In use now**.

Agent CLIs and other terminal programs that support it match your theme too.

#### Your themes

**Your themes** lists the themes you have added, with 2 more tiles, **Browse gallery** and **Create a theme**. **Open themes folder**, beside the heading, opens the folder that holds your themes, `~/.kepler/themes`. Each [profile](/kepler/kepler-profiles) other than the default keeps its own themes folder.

A theme file follows these rules:

- It is a `.json` or `.jsonc` file, so comments are allowed.
- A single file can hold a family of up to 8 themes, such as a dark and a light version.
- Each theme has an id and a name, and `extends` one of Kepler's base themes: `midnight`, `dark`, or `light`. The theme then overrides that base's colors, and can add code colors and a `terminal` block.
- The `terminal` block sets the terminal's background, foreground, cursor, selection, and 16 ANSI colors.

Kepler reads up to 64 theme files, and reloads a file each time you save it.

If Kepler cannot fully read a theme's file, its tile shows **Has problems** or **Has warnings**. To see what is wrong, click the badge. Each problem gives its line and column, or names the setting it is in, such as *themes.1.extends*.

A file with warnings still works. Kepler leaves out a theme that has errors, and still loads the other themes in its file. To fix a file, use one of these options below the list of problems:

- **Create a task to fix it** gives the file to an agent.
- In the desktop app, **Open file** opens the file in your editor, at the error's line when there is one. Changes apply when you save.

A tile's **More actions for *theme*** menu has **Show in folder** and **Move to Trash** (**Move to Recycle Bin** on Windows).

#### Theme gallery

**Browse gallery** opens the **Theme gallery** of community themes, each checked for contrast, which you can try before you install. The gallery needs an internet connection. It has the following controls:

- **Search themes**, which matches a theme's name, author, tags, or description.
- **Show**, which filters to **All**, **Dark**, or **Light** themes.
- **Sort:**, with **Featured**, **Newest**, or **Name**.

Click a theme to see its details card, with its author, its dark and light variants, its version, its license, and any contrast warnings. Then choose one of the following:

- **Install** adds the theme to **Your themes** without changing the theme on screen. The button then reads **Use**.
- **Try it** closes the gallery and paints the whole window in the theme, so you can open a diff or a terminal to judge it. In the bar at the bottom, click **Use *theme***, or **Done** to return to the gallery.

If a theme you already have uses the same id, Kepler asks before it replaces that file, and moves the old file to the Trash. A gallery theme you installed and have not edited offers **Update to *version*** on its tile when a newer version is published. The gallery's themes come from `gitkraken/kepler-themes` on GitHub, where you can also publish your own.

#### Create a theme

**Create a theme** opens the **New task** composer with a prompt already written for an agent, ending in *The theme I want:* for you to describe it. You do not need to attach the themes folder: the agent checks the theme's format and contrast, then saves it to **Your themes**. **Create a task to fix it**, on a broken theme file, starts the same kind of task with that file's problems listed.

#### Themes in a remote window

Themes and your choice of theme belong to this computer. Every window lists and installs themes in this computer's themes folder and gallery, including a window connected to a remote environment.

In a window connected to another machine, the picker adds an **On *host*** group with that machine's themes:

- A theme you do not have offers **Install *theme* on this computer**.
- A theme that differs from your copy offers to update or replace your copy, and is marked **Update to *version***, **Older than yours**, or **Differs from yours**.

Kepler asks before it updates or replaces your copy, and moves your copy to the Trash (the Recycle Bin on Windows). It never replaces your copy on its own.

### Dashboard

**Dashboard views** sets where the Dashboard's views sit, how they look, and whether quiet items dim:

| Setting | What it controls | Default | Options |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Views** | Where the Dashboard's views sit in the window | Top | Top, Left |
| **View style** | How views at the top look | Tabs | Tabs, Pills |
| **Size** | How big views along the left side are | Default | Default, Compact |
| **Counts on views** | Shows how many tasks match each view's filters | On | On, Off |
| **Dim quiet items** | Dims an item's title in lists while it is quiet: no agent connected, no new reply, and nothing waiting on you | On | On, Off |

With **Left**, the **Settings** button moves to the bottom of the views.

### Code

These settings set how diffs and code look:

| Setting | What it controls | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Diff layout** | The layout diffs open in: **Stacked** or **Split** | Stacked |
| **Font** › **Family** | The font for diffs, file views, and code in chat. Leave it empty to use the terminal's font | Empty |
| **Font** › **Size** | Text size in diffs and file views, from 10 to 24 | 13 |

To switch a single diff without changing the default, use the layout button on the file's header in the Changes overlay. See [Review What a Coding Agent Changed](/kepler/review-changes).

### Kep

**Seasonal touches**, on by default, lets [Kep](/kepler/kepler-interface#kep) mark seasons and holidays with small extras, such as an outfit or a bit of weather. Turn it off to keep Kep the same all year.

***

## Chat and terminal

Use **Chat and terminal** to set how a session's chat and terminal views look and behave. Kepler saves these settings on this machine. The top of the page shows which mode new sessions start in. To change it, click **Change in Agents**.

### Chat

**Send messages with** chooses the key that sends a message from the chat box: **Enter**, the default, or **Ctrl/⌘ + Enter**. With **Enter**, **Shift + Enter** starts a new line. With **Ctrl/⌘ + Enter**, **Enter** starts a new line. In the browser on a phone or tablet, **Enter** always starts a new line.

The other **Chat** settings set how wide a session's conversation grows and how it scrolls:

| Setting | What it controls | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Conversation width** | How wide the conversation grows in a wide pane: **Narrow**, **Wide**, or **Full width** | Narrow |
| **Scrolling** › **While an agent replies** | **Follow new output** keeps the newest output in view until you scroll up. **Stay on my message** keeps your message in view | Follow new output |
| **Scrolling** › **Return to where I left off when I reopen a session** | Whether a session reopens where you left it | On |

### Terminal

These settings control Kepler's embedded terminals:

| Setting | What it controls | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Font** › **Family** | *Separate fonts with commas. The terminal uses the first one installed on this machine.* | Empty, which uses your platform's standard monospace fonts |
| **Font** › **Size** | Terminal font size in pixels, from 8 to 32 | 13 |
| **Font** › **Line height** | Spacing between lines, from 1 to 2 | 1.2 |
| **Show the message box under terminal sessions** | Adds Kepler's message box, for attachments and voice, under an agent's terminal | Off |
| **Open links with a click** | Opens file, folder, and web links in a terminal without holding **Ctrl/⌘** | Off |

The grayed text in **Family** is an example, not the value in effect. If Kepler cannot find a font you name, the field says so, and the terminal uses the next name in your list. **Family** and **Size** save when you press **Enter** or leave the field. Code views use this family too, unless you set one under [Code](#code).

While the message box is hidden, a Terminal session's status bar has a microphone that dictates into the agent's own input. See [Dictation](#dictation).

#### Embedded terminals

Each Kepler terminal belongs to a worktree. Opening a terminal starts a shell in that worktree's folder, so you do not need to `cd` into it, and the shell loads your profile the same way an interactive login shell would. Use **Ctrl/⌘ + J** to show and hide the terminal panel, **New terminal** to open another terminal, and **Close terminal** to end one.

Use terminals for work next to an agent session: running tests while the agent writes code, checking Git state, or reproducing something the session did not show. A terminal starts in one worktree and stays there, so for work that spans several repositories, use a standalone terminal.

### Ask Kepler panel

**Auto-hide the floating panel**, off by default, closes the floating [Ask Kepler](/kepler/ask-kepler) panel when you click or move focus elsewhere in Kepler. A docked panel stays open.

***

## Notifications

Use **Notifications** to choose which agent events Kepler tells you about, and where. **Desktop** notifications show while Kepler is in the background, and **In Kepler** alerts show while you are using it. A phone you open Kepler on can notify you too. Sessions started outside Kepler notify you only once they are on a task. Kepler saves these settings on this machine.

### What to notify you about

**What to notify you about** has a **Desktop** and an **In Kepler** box for each event. The following table lists the events and their defaults in the desktop app:

| Event | When it fires | Desktop | In Kepler |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Replies** | *An agent finished replying and it's your turn.* | Off | Off |
| **Questions** | *An agent asks you something and waits for your answer.* Also fires when a plan is ready for your review | On | On |
| **Permission requests** | *An agent wants permission to do something.* | On | On |
| **Approval requests** | *An agent asks to do something in Kepler only you can approve, like deleting a worktree or rewriting a branch.* See [Settings → Approvals](/kepler/settings-approvals) | On | On |
| **Errors** | *A session stops because something went wrong.* | On | On |
| **Usage limits** | *When an agent reaches an account's usage limit.* | On | On |
| **Offers** | *An agent offers to show you a task, session or note.* | Off | On |

In a browser connected to Kepler, every **Desktop** box starts off. Until you set **Approval requests** yourself, it follows **Permission requests**, and **Usage limits** follows **Errors** the same way. When you turn on the first **Desktop** box, Kepler sends a sample notification so your OS asks for permission. Once a phone has notifications turned on, the grid adds a **Phone** column.

These settings appear under the grid:

| Setting | What it controls | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Play a sound with desktop notifications** | Whether a desktop notification makes the OS notification sound | On |
| **Notify even for the task you're looking at** | *Otherwise Kepler stays quiet about the task open in the window you're using.* | Off |
| **Show a count on the app icon** | *Shows how many tasks need you on the Dock icon or taskbar button.* Desktop app only | On |

To silence desktop notifications from one remote machine only, use **Mute notifications from *host*** on that machine in [Remote environments](/kepler/settings-environment#remote-environments).

### Notifications on this phone

When you open Kepler on your phone through [Remote Access](/kepler/settings-environment#remote-access), its **Settings → Notifications** page adds **Notifications on this phone**. Turn on **Notify this phone**, and Kepler notifies the phone when a session needs you and you're away from your computer. To check that notifications arrive, tap **Send a test**.

Phone notifications need the Remote Access link. On an iPhone, add Kepler to your Home Screen from Safari's **Share** menu first, then turn notifications on from the Home Screen app. See [Approve Coding Agent Requests from Your Phone](/kepler/kepler-approve-agent-requests-from-your-phone).

***

## Voice

Use **Voice** to talk to your agents instead of typing, and to have their replies read aloud. Both run on this machine, so nothing you say or hear leaves it. Kepler saves these settings on this machine.

### Check your setup

**Check your setup** tests your devices with the speech model and voice picked on the page:

- Pick the **Microphone** dictation listens to, then click **Try dictation** to see your words as you speak.
- Pick the **Speaker** that Kokoro reads replies on, then click **Play a reply**.

Nothing you say in the test is sent to an agent. Each device you pick is saved for this window. If it is not connected later, Kepler uses the system default and tells you.

### Dictation

Dictation is the microphone in the chat prompt, and on a Terminal session's status bar. It turns on once a speech model is downloaded. To choose and download one, see [Set up dictation in Settings](/kepler/voice-input#set-up-dictation-in-settings).

| Setting | What it controls | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Speech model** | The on-device model that dictates: **Qwen3-ASR** (with a **Qwen3-ASR size**), **Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3**, or **Whisper** (with a **Whisper quality**). Each row has **Download**, and **Remove…** once downloaded | None until you download one |
| **Dictation language** | With Qwen3-ASR, the language you speak. Parakeet and Whisper detect it, so the setting is unavailable with them | Auto-detect |
| **Dictation mode** | **Type as you talk**, **Type when you stop**, or **Send when you stop** | Type as you talk |
| **Vocabulary** | The words dictation learned from your fixes, which **Manage** opens, with Qwen3-ASR only. See [Teach dictation your words](/kepler/voice-input#teach-dictation-your-words) | No words yet |

**Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3** understands English and 24 other European languages. Kepler offers it only on a graphics card with WebGPU and 16-bit float shader support.

To change the speech model, the dictation mode, or the dictation language from a session, right-click its microphone.

### Read aloud

**Read aloud** reads agent replies to you in a chat or a Terminal session, one reply at a time or continuously as new replies arrive. To use it, see [Read aloud](/kepler/voice-input#read-aloud).

| Setting | What it controls | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Speech model** | **System**, or **Kokoro**, natural English voices that need a download | System |
| **Voice** | The voice that reads | System default |
| **Speed** | How fast Kepler reads | 1x |

***

## Keyboard shortcuts

Use **Keyboard shortcuts** to look up Kepler's shortcuts and choose your own keys. The page lists every command in 6 groups: **General**, **Navigation**, **Dashboard**, **Task page**, **Chat**, and **Changes and code views**. A command without a key shows **None**. Menu items and button tooltips show each command's keys, including the ones you set. For a few tab shortcuts that Settings does not list, such as reopening a closed tab and jumping to a tab by position, see [Task View](/kepler/task-view#keyboard).

### Change a shortcut

1. Find the command, or type its name in **Search shortcuts**.
2. Click the pencil (**Change shortcut**) on its row. If the command already has a key, a menu opens: choose **Change shortcut**, **Add another shortcut**, or **Remove** followed by the key.
3. Press the new keys. **Escape** cancels, and **Backspace** removes the shortcut.

You can also start from the command palette: a command's **Change shortcut** action opens this page at that command, ready for the new keys.

If the keys already belong to another command, Kepler names it, and **Replace** moves the keys to this command. Kepler refuses keys it needs elsewhere, such as the key that sends chat messages, and says why.

A changed row offers **Reset to default**. **Changed only** lists only the shortcuts you changed, and **Reset all shortcuts** puts every shortcut back to its default after you confirm. A row with a lock, such as **Copy the selection or the focused item** or **Dismiss / Cancel**, cannot be changed.

### Default shortcuts

The tables list the default keys.

#### General shortcuts

The **General** group holds app-wide shortcuts:

| Action | Shortcut |
|---|---|
| Open settings | Ctrl/⌘ + , |
| Toggle Ask Kepler chat | Ctrl/⌘ + K or Ctrl/⌘ + L |
| Toggle Ask Kepler terminal | Ctrl + ` |
| New Ask Kepler chat | Ctrl/⌘ + Shift + K or Ctrl/⌘ + Shift + L |
| New task | Ctrl/⌘ + N |
| Open quick launcher (global) | Shift + Alt/⌥ + N |
| New window | Ctrl/⌘ + Shift + N |
| Quit | Ctrl/⌘ + Q |
| Zoom in | Ctrl/⌘ + = |
| Zoom out | Ctrl/⌘ + - |
| Reset zoom | Ctrl/⌘ + 0 |
| Toggle full screen | F11, or ⌘ + ⌃ + F on macOS |
| Minimize | Ctrl/⌘ + M |
| Reload | Ctrl/⌘ + R |
| Hide Kepler | ⌘ + H (macOS only) |
| Hide others | ⌘ + ⌥ + H (macOS only) |
| Copy the selection or the focused item | Ctrl/⌘ + C |
| Close window | Ctrl/⌘ + Shift + W |
| Toggle terminal | Ctrl/⌘ + J |
| New session | Ctrl/⌘ + T |
| Rename task | F2 |
| Delete task | Ctrl/⌘ + Shift + Backspace |
| Manage remote environments | Ctrl/⌘ + Shift + R |
| Toggle side panel | Ctrl/⌘ + B |
| Open file | Ctrl/⌘ + O |
| Open folder | Ctrl/⌘ + Shift + O |
| Go to file | Ctrl/⌘ + P |
| Go to task or command | Ctrl/⌘ + Shift + P or F1 |
| Change search scope | Alt + S, or ⌘ + ⌥ + S on macOS |
| Dismiss / Cancel | Escape |

**Go to task or command** and **Open folder** are also in the app menu, as **View › Command Palette…** and **File › Open Folder…**.

#### Navigation shortcuts

The **Navigation** group moves you between tasks, tabs, and regions:

| Action | Shortcut |
|---|---|
| Go to next in Needs attention | None |
| Go to next in Unread | None |
| Go to what needs you next | F8 |
| Previous tab | Ctrl/⌘ + Shift + [, or Ctrl + PageUp on Windows and Linux |
| Next tab | Ctrl/⌘ + Shift + ], or Ctrl + PageDown on Windows and Linux |
| Move tab left | Ctrl/⌘ + Alt/⌥ + [, or Ctrl + Shift + PageUp on Windows and Linux |
| Move tab right | Ctrl/⌘ + Alt/⌥ + ], or Ctrl + Shift + PageDown on Windows and Linux |
| Focus next region | F6 |
| Focus previous region | Shift + F6 |
| Close tab or panel | Ctrl/⌘ + W, or Ctrl + F4 on Windows and Linux |
| Go back | Alt + ←, or ⌘ + [ on macOS |
| Go forward | Alt + →, or ⌘ + ] on macOS |

**Go to next in Needs attention** opens the next session waiting on you, and **Go to next in Unread** opens the next unread reply. **Go to what needs you next** (**F8**) does both, waiting sessions first, and skips what is already on screen. **F8** works even from a focused terminal.

#### Dashboard shortcuts

The **Dashboard** group works on the Dashboard's tasks and detail panels:

| Action | Shortcut |
|---|---|
| Move panel left | Ctrl/⌘ + Alt/⌥ + Shift + ← |
| Move panel right | Ctrl/⌘ + Alt/⌥ + Shift + → |
| Move panel up | Ctrl/⌘ + Alt/⌥ + Shift + ↑ |
| Move panel down | Ctrl/⌘ + Alt/⌥ + Shift + ↓ |
| Move task to the previous Progress stage | Ctrl/⌘ + Shift + ← |
| Move task to the next Progress stage | Ctrl/⌘ + Shift + → |
| Focus detail panel 1 to 8 | Ctrl/⌘ + 1 to Ctrl/⌘ + 8 |
| Focus last detail panel | Ctrl/⌘ + 9 |
| Previous item in list | Alt/⌥ + Shift + ↑ |
| Next item in list | Alt/⌥ + Shift + ↓ |
| Switch to older panel | Ctrl + Shift + Tab |
| Switch to newer panel | Ctrl + Tab |
| Solo detail panel | Ctrl/⌘ + Shift + M |
| Maximize panel terminals | Ctrl/⌘ + Shift + J |
| Toggle changes pane | Ctrl/⌘ + Shift + G |
| Toggle task list peek | Ctrl/⌘ + Shift + B |
| Toggle resources pane | Ctrl/⌘ + Shift + E |
| Find in dashboard | Ctrl/⌘ + F |
| Dashboard: Find from the list | / |
| Dashboard: Your groups | Shift + G |
| Dashboard: Next row | J |
| Dashboard: Previous row | K |
| Dashboard: Open task page | O |
| Dashboard: Star or unstar task | I |
| Dashboard: Mark task read or unread | U |
| Dashboard: Archive or restore task | E |
| Dashboard: Put task on hold or back to automatic | H |
| Dashboard: Set task progress | S |
| Dashboard: Add task to a group or change its group | G |
| Dashboard: Rename task | R |
| Dashboard: Open task actions | . |
| Dashboard: Add task to selection or remove it | X |
| Dashboard: Select tasks up to this one | Shift + X |
| Dashboard: Delete task | Delete or Backspace |

From **Dashboard: Next row** on, the keys act on the focused task row in a Tasks view, or on the selected tasks. **Dashboard: Find from the list** focuses the Dashboard's search. None of the **Dashboard:** keys can be changed.

#### Task page shortcuts

The **Task page** group works on a task's page:

| Action | Shortcut |
|---|---|
| Focus chat | Ctrl/⌘ + 1 |
| Focus changes | Ctrl/⌘ + 2 |
| Focus resources | Ctrl/⌘ + 3 |
| Switch sessions | Ctrl + Tab |
| Switch sessions, oldest first | Ctrl + Shift + Tab |
| Maximize terminal drawer | Ctrl/⌘ + Shift + J |
| Show or hide the preview in Add resources | Ctrl/⌘ + Alt/⌥ + P |

#### Chat shortcuts

The **Chat** group works in a session's conversation:

| Action | Shortcut |
|---|---|
| Find in conversation | Ctrl/⌘ + F |
| Previous message | Ctrl/⌘ + Alt/⌥ + ↑ |
| Next message | Ctrl/⌘ + Alt/⌥ + ↓ |
| Interrupt & send | Ctrl/⌘ + Shift + Enter |
| Send after this turn | Alt/⌥ + Enter |
| Switch between terminal and reading view | Ctrl/⌘ + Shift + X |
| Toggle dictation | Ctrl/⌘ + Shift + Space |
| Read the last reply aloud, or pause and resume it | None |

**Toggle dictation** starts or stops dictation in the focused message box that has a microphone, including the **New task** composer and a Terminal session. **Read the last reply aloud, or pause and resume it** works on the focused session.

#### Changes and code view shortcuts

This group has 2 lists. The **Changes** list works in the Changes view:

| Action | Shortcut |
|---|---|
| Filter changed files | Ctrl/⌘ + P |
| Previous file | Alt/⌥ + ↑ |
| Next file | Alt/⌥ + ↓ |
| Next change | F7 |
| Previous change | Shift + F7 |
| Toggle changes sidebar | Ctrl/⌘ + B |
| Open all changes | Ctrl/⌘ + Shift + A |
| Comment on selection | Ctrl/⌘ + Shift + C |
| Edit working copy | Ctrl/⌘ + E |

The **Code views** list works in any code view, such as a diff or a file you have opened:

| Action | Shortcut |
|---|---|
| Find in file or diff | Ctrl/⌘ + F |
| Next match | F3, or ⌘ + G on macOS |
| Previous match | Shift + F3, or ⌘ + Shift + G on macOS |
| Match case | Alt + C, or ⌘ + ⌥ + C on macOS |
| Match whole word | Alt + W, or ⌘ + ⌥ + W on macOS |
| Use regular expression | Alt + R, or ⌘ + ⌥ + R on macOS |
| Find only in changes | Alt + L, or ⌘ + ⌥ + L on macOS |

### Shortcuts that depend on where you are

Some keys do different things depending on where you are:

- **Ctrl/⌘ + 1**, **Ctrl/⌘ + 2**, and **Ctrl/⌘ + 3** focus a detail panel on the Dashboard but a column on the task page.
- **Ctrl + Tab** switches detail panels on the Dashboard and sessions on the task page.
- **Ctrl/⌘ + Shift + [** and **Ctrl/⌘ + Shift + ]** step through the Dashboard's views on the Dashboard, and through a panel's tabs when the panel or the task page has focus. **Ctrl/⌘ + Alt/⌥ + [** and **Ctrl/⌘ + Alt/⌥ + ]** move the current view or tab.
- **Ctrl/⌘ + Shift + J** maximizes the panel's terminals on the Dashboard and the terminal drawer on the task page.
- **Ctrl/⌘ + B** shows or hides the changes panel in the Changes view. On the Dashboard it docks or hides the task list, and on the task page it docks or hides the context panel.
- **Ctrl/⌘ + P** filters changed files in the Changes view and opens **Go to file** elsewhere.
- **Ctrl/⌘ + F** finds in the Dashboard from its list or header, finds in a file or diff in a code view, and finds in the conversation elsewhere.
- **Ctrl/⌘ + Shift + G** shows or hides changes in a Dashboard detail panel, and, on macOS, moves to the previous match in a code view.
- **Ctrl/⌘ + C** on a focused row, chip, or link copies what it names, such as a task's Kepler link, a pull request link, an issue link, a file path, or a commit hash. In a text field, a terminal, or a text selection, it copies as usual.

**Previous item in list** and **Next item in list** work even while you type in the open panel's chat.

**Open quick launcher** works while Kepler is in the background. Its row has a **Global** badge. **Close tab or panel**, **Toggle full screen**, **Minimize**, and **Reload** work only in the desktop app.

On Windows and Linux, a focused terminal passes **Ctrl + W**, **Ctrl + L**, and **Ctrl + B** to the shell. To toggle the Ask Kepler chat from a terminal, press **Ctrl + K**: the shell does not keep that key. **Ctrl + `** always toggles the Ask Kepler terminal, even from a terminal.

Hold the **Go back** or **Go forward** key to keep moving through your history.

**Send feedback**, **Show release notes**, **Show About Kepler**, **Check for updates**, and **Clean up worktrees** have no default key, nor do commands such as **Open documentation**, **Appearance: Dark**, and **Dashboard layout: Board**. To use one from the keyboard, give it a key on this page.

***

---

---
# Environment Settings
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/settings-environment/
product: Kepler
feature: Settings
content_type: reference
audience: developer
plan_required: all
status: GA
last_verified: 2026-11

Use **Settings → Remote environments** to save the machines your agents can run on over SSH or WSL, and to choose how remote windows load. Use **Settings → Remote Access** to open this computer's Kepler from a browser or your phone. To learn how to work in a remote environment day to day, see [Remote Environments](/kepler/remote-environments).

***

## Remote environments

Run your agents on another machine, such as a dev server or cloud VM, while you work from here. Kepler installs itself over SSH, so you do not need to set up anything on that machine first. On Windows, you can also use a WSL distro, with nothing extra to install.

To open this page from anywhere, press **Ctrl/⌘ + Shift + R**, or click **Manage remote environments…** in the remote chip's popover. Kepler saves the machine list on this computer, whichever machine a window is connected to.

The Remote environments page has 3 sections:

| Section | What it holds |
|---|---|
| **Your machines** | Your saved machines. Each row shows whether the machine is connected and how many windows have it open |
| **Found on this machine** | Machines from your SSH config and WSL that you have not added yet. The section appears only while Kepler finds one |
| **Remote windows** | How a window connected to another machine loads its interface. See [Remote windows](#remote-windows) |

In **Your machines**, you can do the following:

- To open a machine in this window, click **Connect**. To open it in a new window, click the window icon next to **Connect**.
- To add a machine by hand, click **Add machine**. On Windows, choose **SSH** or **WSL** in **Machine type**. A WSL machine takes a **Distro** and an optional **Name**.

In **Found on this machine**, you can do the following:

- To save a machine, click **Add**.
- To move a machine out of the list, click **Hide**. Hidden machines appear under **Show hidden (*N*)**.

To open a saved machine's page, click the machine:

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| Name | Rename the machine. You can rename a machine only from a local window |
| **Latency**, **Live sessions** | The connection's current state |
| **Color** | Tints the machine's chip, its popover, and a connected window's top strip, so you can tell machines apart. **None** removes the tint |
| **Mute notifications from *machine*** | Stops desktop notifications for sessions on the machine. Alerts still appear inside its windows |
| **Connection** | Edit the SSH or WSL address. If you enter a new SSH address, Kepler asks you to trust its host key with **Trust and save** |
| **Remove *machine*…** | Deletes the saved machine |

To edit the connection of a machine you are connected to, disconnect from it first.

In a window connected to an SSH machine, a **Ports** list shows the ports forwarded from that machine to this computer. You can do the following:

- To forward another port, enter its number.
- To stop forwarding a port, click **Stop**.
- To stop every forwarded port, click **Stop all**. This button appears when more than one port is forwarded.

A window connected to a machine shows the other machines read-only. To add, edit, or remove machines, click **Open in a local window**.

If a window cannot reconnect to its machine, it shows a full-screen recovery screen instead of this page. See [The recovery screen](/kepler/remote-environments#the-recovery-screen).

### Remote windows

When another machine runs a different version of Kepler, a window connected to it still uses this app's interface. To show that machine's interface instead, turn off the following setting, in the desktop app only:

| Setting | What it controls | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Always use this app's interface** | Offers to update the server or this app instead of showing the server's interface. An outdated server then updates when you connect, even while other devices use it | On |

To learn how to connect, forward ports, and how sessions behave on a machine, see [Remote environments](/kepler/remote-environments).

***

## Remote Access

Remote Access lets you use this machine from any browser or your phone, through a secure GitKraken relay. You do not need to open a port or set up a tunnel.

Under **How it works**, the page lists 3 steps:

1. Turn it on and name this machine.
2. Scan the QR code or open the link that appears here, on your phone or any browser.
3. Sign in with your GitKraken account, and this machine's tasks and sessions are there.

### Turning Remote Access on and off

To turn on Remote Access, do the following:

1. Click **Turn on Remote Access**.
2. Enter a name in **Name this machine**.

A status badge shows the connection state, such as **Active** or **Waiting to reconnect**. While Remote Access is on, the page shows a QR code to scan with your phone and **Copy URL**. This machine stays awake while Remote Access is on. To change that, click **Change in Agents**, which opens [Keep agents running](/kepler/settings-agents#keep-agents-running).

A phone you pair can also get notifications when a session needs you. Turn them on from the phone, in its **Settings → Notifications**. See [Notifications on this phone](/kepler/settings-app#notifications-on-this-phone).

Remote Access stays on until you turn it off, sign out, or another account signs in.

To turn off Remote Access, click the switch, then confirm. Every paired device is disconnected.

### Reconnecting after a dropped connection

If Remote Access loses the connection, Kepler first retries quickly. It then shows **Waiting to reconnect** and the reason, under **Unable to connect**, with *Kepler retries every 5 minutes.* To retry at once, click **Retry now**. Paired devices stay paired.

These 2 reasons tell you how to fix them:

- *Waiting for a GitKraken sign-in. Remote Access connects as soon as one is available.*
- *Your account has reached its limit of machines with Remote Access on. Remove one you no longer use, then retry.* This message has a **Manage machines on gitkraken.dev** button.

### Managing machines and devices

To see every machine on your account with Remote Access on, and remove the ones you no longer use, click **Manage machines on gitkraken.dev** under **Machines on your account**. The button appears even while Remote Access is off.

**Connected devices** lists each device that has connected. It marks **This device**, shows when each device was **Last seen**, and marks a device that **Gets notifications**. You can do the following:

- To disconnect one device, click **Revoke**.
- To reload the list, click **Refresh**.

Only you can connect, signed in to your GitKraken account.

A pairing link works once and expires after 5 minutes. A used link shows *This pairing link no longer works*. To pair again, open a new link from the computer running Kepler. If you open a saved address, such as a bookmark, after its browser session has ended, Kepler takes you to gitkraken.dev to sign in again. To learn about prerequisites, pairing, and managing sessions from gitkraken.dev, see [Remote environments](/kepler/remote-environments).

***

---

---
# Update and Help Settings
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/settings-updates-help/
product: Kepler
feature: Settings
content_type: reference
audience: developer
plan_required: all
status: GA
last_verified: 2026-11

Use **Updates** to see which version of Kepler you have, to install a new one, and to keep your agents up to date. Use **Help** to open the docs and release notes, see dismissed tips again, and save Kepler's logs when you need to report a problem.

## Updates

The **Updates** page has these rows:

| Row | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Current version** | The installed version, with **Release notes** beside it to open what's new in that release |
| **Check for updates** | Checks for a newer release and downloads it in the background. Reads **Up to date** when there is nothing newer, and becomes **Check again** |
| Download progress | While a release downloads, shows its progress and the time left |
| **New version** | Appears once a release is ready, with **Restart to update** beside it, and how many running agents a restart would stop |

When an update is ready, a chip also appears in the top bar on every screen. Its popover reads **Update ready to install** and says what a restart does to running work. If agents are in the middle of a tool call when you restart, Kepler waits up to 30 seconds for them to finish. To skip the wait, click **Restart now**, which may interrupt tool calls that are still running.

**Check for updates** in the app menu shows its result where you are, without opening Settings. The top bar shows **Checking…**, then **Up to date** or the download. On the welcome screen, click the version in the corner to check. If that check fails, it reads **Unable to check for updates** with **Try again**.

After an update, the release notes open in Kepler by themselves, once any guided start has ended. A release can start with a highlights card, and each item opens its part of the notes.

The update controls appear only in the desktop app. In a browser window connected to Kepler, the **Updates** page has nothing to update.

### Agent updates

Kepler checks the agent CLIs you have installed for newer versions. **Agent updates** reads **All agents are up to date**, or lists the updates available with **Update all**. When an update is available, a button also appears in the title bar, with **Update all** and **Skip these versions**. These settings choose how Kepler tells you:

| Setting | What it controls | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Show agent updates in the title bar** | *A button appears in the title bar when an installed agent has a newer version. Settings still marks each agent either way.* | On |
| **Show a restart notice on outdated sessions** | *After an agent or Kepler updates, a notice above each open chat or terminal session still on the old version offers to restart it.* | On |

***

## Help

Use **Help** to find the docs and release notes, see tips again, and save logs when something goes wrong.

### Help

The **Help** section links to the docs and release notes, and shows again any tip you dismissed:

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Kepler documentation** | *Guides, keyboard shortcuts, and agent setup.* **Open docs** opens the Kepler docs site in your browser |
| **Release notes** | *See what changed in each version.* **Show release notes** opens them in Kepler, starting with the release's highlights when it has them. See [Updates](#updates) |
| **Show tips and guides again** | A disclosure, closed by default: *Kepler points out a few controls the first time they matter. Show any of those tips again here.* |

Inside the disclosure, each tip has a row with its own **Show again** button. The tips are the following:

- **Actions callout**
- **Todo pointer**
- **Task page callout**
- **Panel layout callout**

To show every tip again at once, instead of 1 row at a time, click **Reset all onboarding and show everything again** at the bottom of the disclosure.

### Logs

To report a problem, save the logs and attach the file. The **Logs** section has these controls:

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Copy path** | Copies the current log's path to your clipboard |
| **Show in Finder** | Opens the log's folder in your file manager (**Show in Explorer** on Windows, **Show in file manager** on Linux). Hidden where the machine cannot open a file manager |
| **Save logs…** | Saves Kepler's logs as a single zip file |
| **Clear log…** | Deletes the current and rotated log files, after a confirmation |

In a window connected to a remote environment, the section shows the remote machine's logs. Saving them from there includes this machine's logs too. To open your local logs, click **Show this machine's logs**.

To find this computer's log without opening Settings, use **Help → Show Logs in Finder** (**Show Logs in Explorer**, **Show Logs in File Manager**) in the app menu.

---

---
# Remote Environments
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/remote-environments/
product: Kepler
feature: Remote Environments
content_type: how-to
audience: developer
plan_required: all
status: GA
last_verified: 2026-11

A **remote environment** runs your agents, worktrees, and terminals on another machine: a dev server, a cloud VM, or a WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux) instance on Windows, while you work from this window. Kepler installs itself on the host over SSH (Secure Shell), so you do not need to pre-install anything there.

***

## Two remote features

Kepler has 2 remote features, and they work in opposite directions:

| Feature | Direction | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| **Remote environments** | Kepler on your desktop reaches **out** to another machine, and your work runs there | The title-bar chip, and **Settings → Remote environments** |
| **Remote Access** | Another device reaches **in** to this Kepler, and your work stays here | The **Remote Access** button in the title bar, and **Settings → Remote Access** |

Both sit at the left of the title bar, right after **New task**. The **Remote Access** button shows a monitor-and-phone icon.

To let another device reach this Kepler, rather than connecting *to* another machine, see [Remote Access](#remote-access-reach-kepler-from-another-device).

***

## Switching environments from the title bar

Each window works on one environment at a time, and the title-bar chip shows which one. The chip leads with the environment's type icon, and a green dot on that icon means connected.

| Chip | What it means |
|---|---|
| The computer icon alone | This window works on this machine. Hover over it to see **Local** |
| **Connecting to *machine*…**, or the current stage | This window is connecting, or its server is restarting or updating |
| **Reconnecting…** | The connection dropped and Kepler is rebuilding it |
| Host name | Connected. The chip takes the host's [color](#host-details) when you have set one |
| Brand fill with an up-arrow | Connected, and a newer server build is ready for the host |
| Warning triangle | The app and the server disagree on version; the popover says which side to update |
| Radio-tower glyph | This window is [forwarding ports](#port-forwarding) from the host |
| An error headline | The last attempt failed; the host's Settings page keeps the full error |

**Hover over the chip to preview the popover.** To open the whole popover and keep it open, click the chip, or focus it and press **Enter** or **Down Arrow**.

### The popover

Use the popover to see which machine this window is on, switch to another machine, and open Settings to manage your machines.

| Part | What it does |
|---|---|
| Header | The current machine, with its address, latency, and versions, or this window's connection progress or failure |
| Gear (**Machine settings**) | Opens the machine's Settings page |
| **Restart server to update** | Appears when a newer server build is ready. See [Server controls](#server-controls) |
| **Disconnect** | Disconnects this window only. The server keeps its sessions running |
| **Restart server** (circular arrow) | Restarts a connected server when no update is pending. See [Server controls](#server-controls) |
| **Stop server** | Stops the server on the machine until you start it again. Every other window connected to it moves to the [recovery screen](#the-recovery-screen) ([When you stop a server](#when-you-stop-a-server)) |
| Forwarded ports | Lists the ports this window forwards, and opens the host's **Ports** list |
| **Switch to** | Every other saved host, plus **Local** (*Work on this machine*) when this window is on a remote |
| **Found on this machine** | WSL distributions found on this PC, offered for one-click connect while you have no saved hosts |
| **Manage remote environments…** | Opens **Settings → Remote environments**. **Ctrl/⌘ + Shift + R** |

The line under **Restart server to update** says what the update will stop. When nothing would stop, the update starts at once. Otherwise, the **Update server?** confirmation names the agents and terminals that stop, or says that the server could not report them.

If this app is older than the server, the header offers an update for this app instead, and says that sessions on the host keep running.

To move this window to another host, click the host's row under **Switch to**. To open the host in a new window and leave this window where it is, hold **Ctrl/⌘** while you click, or click the window icon at the end of the row. A host already open in another window is marked **Connected**. Clicking its row brings that window to the front instead of opening a second connection.

A host under **Switch to** can have profiles from another computer but no server for this profile yet. Its row then says how many profiles it has. When you connect, Kepler asks whether to start this profile on the host, with its own server and tasks, or to open one of the host's profiles on this computer. See [Profiles on your other machines](/kepler/kepler-profiles#profiles-on-your-other-machines).

***

## Windows on a remote host

- **New Window opens on the same host.** **File → New Window** (**Ctrl/⌘ + Shift + N**) from a remote window opens a second window on that host. A remote window also offers **File → New Local Window** when you want a local one. A new window that cannot reach the host opens on the [recovery screen](#the-recovery-screen) with the reason.
- **Windows on one host share a connection,** so another window on it opens quickly.
- **A host open in another window shows as connected.** The popover and Settings offer **Show window**, and show its latency, versions, and sessions.
- **The last closed remote window reopens on its host.** With no window open, the dock, the tray, or launching Kepler again reconnects to the host the last window was on. If you close a window that was still waiting on an unreachable host, the next window opens locally. If **Restore windows on launch** is off, Kepler launches locally.
- **A link opens on its machine.** A task or session link copied in a window on a remote machine opens on that machine, in a new window if none is open there. A link copied in a local window opens in the window you used last. If a link cannot open on its machine, it opens on this computer instead, and starts nothing by itself. If the item is not found on that machine, the notice offers **Open on this computer**.

***

## Managing machines in Settings

Use **Settings → Remote environments** to add, connect, edit, and remove machines. In a local window, **Your machines** lists your saved machines. Each row shows the host's type, whether it is connected, and how many windows already use it. From a row, you can do the following:

- To connect this window, click **Connect**.
- To connect in a new window, click the window icon.
- To bring forward a host that is open in another window, click **Show window**, which replaces **Connect** for that host.
- To open the host's page, click the row.

**Found on this machine** lists machines from your `~/.ssh/config` and WSL distributions you have not saved yet. To save one, click **Add**. To stop Kepler from offering a machine, click its eye icon to hide it. To bring hidden machines back, click **Show hidden (*N*)**.

### Host details

A host's page has a card of actions at the top:

- **Connect**. To connect in a new window, **Ctrl/⌘**-click it. While a connection is in progress, the same button cancels it.
- **Show window** and **Connect to *machine* in a new window**, in place of **Connect**, when another window already has the host open.
- **Stop server**.
- **Remove *machine*…**, the red trash icon.

To rename the saved connection, click the pencil beside the name. Renaming changes nothing on the host.

| Group | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Connection** | Edits **Host**, **Port**, **User**, and **Identity file** for SSH, or **Distro** for WSL. Disconnect first: the fields are locked while the host is connected |
| **Color** | Tints the host's chip, its rows, and the top bar of its windows with one of the 12 task-group colors |
| **Mute notifications from *machine*** | Stops desktop notifications for sessions on the machine; alerts still appear inside its windows |
| **Sessions** | Lists the host's live agent sessions; click one to open it. For a host nobody is connected to, **Check** shows what is running there |

When you change the address of a host that the SSH wizard created, Kepler first fetches the new address's host key and shows it under **New host key**. **Trust and save** pins that key and saves the host in one step. When you change any address, Kepler notes that an install at the old address stays there.

**Kepler reads your own `~/.ssh/config` before it offers to write to it.** Kepler uses a host you have already configured exactly as you configured it, including its user, port, identity file, jump host, and any other settings. Kepler offers to edit the file only when it has nothing there to reuse. **Open in → VS Code** on an SSH environment uses that same host entry, so VS Code connects the way your terminal does.

### Server controls

The restart and update controls act on the server a window is connected to, so they appear in the popover and in a remote window's Settings. **Stop server** is also on every host's page in a local window.

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Restart server to update** | Installs the newer server build and reconnects. When something would stop, the **Update server?** confirmation lists it first |
| **Restart server** | Offered when no update is pending, for a stuck server. It always asks first |
| **Stop server** | Stops the Kepler server on the host for every connected window and device, and ends its agent sessions |
| **Auto-shutdown when idle** | Stops the server after a number of minutes with no window connected and nothing running. Off by default; the timeout defaults to 30 minutes |
| **Stop anyway after** | Stops the server after a number of hours with no window connected, even if work is running. Defaults to 12 hours |

**Auto-shutdown when idle** counts an agent that is working, or a terminal that is running a command, as something running. A shell that waits at its prompt does not count. **Stop anyway after** limits how long running work can keep the server up, so a dev server you forgot about does not keep it running indefinitely. The hours count from when the last window disconnects, and start over when a window connects.

Both settings belong to the machine, so they apply to every window and device connected to it. You set them from a window connected to the machine.

Both the **Update server?** and **Restart server?** confirmations list what a restart would stop, or say that running agents and terminals keep going. A restart reconnects this window and disconnects the other windows on the server. While an update or restart runs, the other server controls wait and say why.

**Keep agents and terminals running after Kepler quits or restarts**, in **Settings → Agents → Keep agents running**, is on by default. While it is on, running agents keep going through a restart or update. **Stop server** ends them either way.

### When you stop a server

A server that you stop on purpose stays stopped. This applies whether you stop it from this window, another window, Settings, or another device. Kepler does not start it again on its own, even when an automatic reconnect, a launch, or reopening the last window would otherwise connect to it. Those windows open on the [recovery screen](#the-recovery-screen), which says the server was stopped.

The server starts again only when you choose one of these actions:

- **Reconnect**, **Connect**, or **Try again**
- **File → New Window** on that machine
- **Restart server to update**

If a window stops its own server or disconnects, the window switches to local without showing the recovery screen.

### From a remote window

In a window that is on a remote, Settings shows only that host:

- Its connected card with the server controls
- **Auto-shutdown when idle**
- **Color** and mute
- Its **Ports** (SSH)
- Your other saved hosts to switch to

A remote window never shows the other hosts' addresses. To rename a host, edit a connection, or add or remove a host, click **Open in a local window**. You also need a local window to switch to a host that needs a password; its row offers **Open in a local window**.

### Connection failures

A failed connection shows an **Unable to connect to *machine*** alert with the SSH diagnostic and a **Copy error** button, so you can paste the diagnostic into a bug report. A failure on another machine does not drop this window's connection.

Common SSH failures, such as **Connection refused** or **Host key verification failed**, get a plain-language headline and a hint. These failures need you to act:

- **Update remote Kepler server**: the host's server is too old to take your GitKraken sign-in. Update the Kepler install on the host and try again.
- **Unable to answer this sign-in**: the machine, or a jump server on the way to it, asked for a password or code Kepler has no answer for. Set up key sign-in for that machine.
- An expired password: change your password on the machine in a terminal, then connect again.
- **The Kepler server on the remote machine is running but not responding**: restart the server, with **Restart server** on the [recovery screen](#the-recovery-screen).
- **The SSH server doesn't allow port forwarding, which Kepler needs**: ask the SSH server's administrator to allow TCP forwarding (`AllowTcpForwarding`) for your account.
- **Unable to install the Kepler server**: the message says why, such as a full disk. Fix that on the machine, then try again. See [How Kepler installs on a remote machine](#how-kepler-installs-on-a-remote-machine).

On a WSL machine, Kepler says when the distro no longer exists, and when Windows cannot reach the Kepler server inside WSL: run `wsl --shutdown` in a terminal, then connect again. Anything else reads **Connection failed**.

If the failure happens while you are adding a host, the wizard shows the headline, the hint, and the diagnostic in place, with **Try again**.

For Kepler's own log file, use **Settings → Help → Logs**.

### Removing a connection

**Remove *machine*…** deletes the saved entry on this desktop. If the SSH wizard created the entry, Kepler also offers to remove what the wizard set up:

| Cleanup option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Remove scoped known_hosts file** | Deletes the host-key trust file Kepler created for this connection | On |
| **Remove generated local SSH key** | Deletes the key the wizard generated, and its `.pub` sibling | On when such a key exists |
| **Uninstall Kepler server on the machine** | Stops the server and removes its install folder on the machine | On, unless the server is in use |
| **Remove deployed key from remote authorized_keys** | Removes the key the wizard installed on the host | Off |

Removing a WSL host offers **Uninstall Kepler server on the machine** for the distro. For a distro that no longer exists, Kepler shows nothing to uninstall.

If the server reports live sessions or connected clients, Kepler disables the uninstall until you select **Uninstall anyway, I understand sessions on this machine may be lost**. If the host is unreachable, or needs a password Kepler does not have, Kepler hides the host-side options, and the dialog states which of the two reasons applies.

***

## Add an SSH host

To add an SSH host, click **Add machine** in **Settings → Remote environments**. On Windows, pick the **Machine type** first: **SSH** or **WSL**. To save a host already in your `~/.ssh/config`, use **Add** under **Found on this machine** instead.

A host taken from `~/.ssh/config` inherits your system SSH configuration, including its host-key trust. A host built in the wizard gets its own trust file, pinned at the fingerprint you accepted.

### The wizard

The SSH wizard has 5 steps:

| Step | What you do |
|---|---|
| *Connect to a machine you reach over SSH…* | **Name** (optional, defaults to its address), **Host**, **User** (optional, defaults to the machine's `$USER`), **Port** |
| *Choose authentication.* | Pick a mode (see below) |
| *Verify the machine's fingerprint.* | Kepler fetches the host key and shows its algorithm and fingerprint. **Trust and continue** pins it |
| *Verifying the connection.* | Kepler makes a real connection before anything is saved |
| *Ready to save.* | **Add** saves the host and opens its page. Nothing connects until you press **Connect**; a password the wizard verified is reused for that first connect |

If the address you enter is a machine you already saved, the first step says so and offers **Use *machine* instead**, which opens the saved machine's page.

| Authentication mode | What it means |
|---|---|
| **Existing key** | Use one of the keys already in `~/.ssh`. Unavailable when Kepler finds none |
| **Use my SSH agent or SSH config** | Sign in the way your terminal does: with keys from ssh-agent, 1Password, Secretive, a security key, or `~/.ssh/config`. The default when the host is a name from `~/.ssh/config`, or when Kepler finds no key files |
| **Password** | *Re-prompt every connect.* The password is never stored |
| **Generate key** | *Keyless after first connect.* Kepler uses the password once to install a fresh ed25519 key at `~/.ssh/id_ed25519_kepler_<hash>`. Your existing keys are never overwritten |

**Generate key** needs `ssh-keygen` on your machine; the chip reads **ssh-keygen missing** when ssh-keygen is absent.

If you pick **Password**, the wizard then offers **Set up a key for this machine?** **Generate and copy key** generates a fresh ed25519 key, copies it to the host, and uses it for future connections, so you do not need the password again. **Skip** keeps the host on password sign-in.

If the host rejects a key-based connection, the host's page shows a password row so you can retry with a password. If no key is saved for that host yet, the page also offers to install one at the same time. When a connection you start needs a password, a passphrase, or a code, Kepler asks for it in the window. See [Signing in to the machine](#signing-in-to-the-machine).

### SSH to a Windows machine

Kepler connects to Windows hosts over SSH as well as Linux and macOS ones. Kepler detects a Windows host and installs itself accordingly.

Nothing changes in the wizard. If the host authenticates but its shell rejects Kepler's commands, the diagnostic reads **Remote shell was unable to run the command**, and the hint points at the OpenSSH default shell. Windows 10 and 11 ship PowerShell, so a changed default shell is the usual cause.

The host-side cleanup offered by **Remove *machine*…** does not run on a Windows host. See [Known limitations](#known-limitations).

***

## WSL environments

On Windows, a WSL 2 distro is a remote environment like any other, and the simplest one to set up: it needs no credentials and no fingerprint check.

- Kepler detects WSL and lists your **version 2** distros. Kepler does not offer WSL 1 distros, or Docker Desktop's own `docker-desktop` and `docker-desktop-data` distros.
- Detected distros appear under **Found on this machine** in Settings, and in the popover while you have no saved hosts, where one click connects to it. Picking one in the popover saves the distro as a host and connects to it, so the connection survives a disconnect.
- To add one by hand, choose **Add machine**, then **WSL** under **Machine type**, and enter its **Distro** (and an optional **Name**). A WSL host is edited, checked, and removed exactly like an SSH one.
- Keep your repositories in the Linux file system, such as your home folder in the distro. Git and agents are slow from WSL on a repository stored on a Windows drive, and the repository's **Edit repo** page shows a warning for one.

***

## Port forwarding

When an agent or a terminal starts a dev server on an SSH host, its `http://localhost:3000` link points at the host, not at this computer. Kepler forwards that port over your SSH connection so the link opens here.

- **Click the link.** In an SSH window, **Ctrl/⌘**-click a `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, or `0.0.0.0` link in a terminal, or click one in the agent transcript. Kepler forwards the port to the host's `localhost`, then opens the local URL. If that port is already taken on this computer, Kepler picks a free one.
- **Open it from the task.** A `localhost` link attached to a task opens through forwarding too, from the task's context panel, the link's detail, or the Dashboard's resources list. Agents attach the URL of a dev server they start for you to open.
- **Add one by hand.** **Settings → Remote environments → Ports**, in the SSH window, lists this window's forwards as remote port → local URL. To add a forward, enter a **Port** and click **Add**. **Stop** ends one forward, and **Stop all** appears when more than one is forwarded.

While anything is forwarded, the chip shows a radio-tower glyph and the popover adds a summary row that opens the **Ports** list.

Forwards belong to the window that made them. Disconnecting, closing, reconnecting, or switching hosts ends them, and Kepler does not restore them. A forward that fails opens nothing rather than reaching a service on this computer. Local and WSL windows open `localhost` links as they are, with no forward.

***

## What runs where

| Piece | Runs on |
|---|---|
| Kepler's window and its native capabilities | Your local machine |
| Git operations, worktrees, and repositories | The host |
| Agent and terminal sessions | The host |
| Provider and issue-tracker data | The host |
| The interface itself | This computer, unless you turn off **Always use this app's interface** (below) |
| Themes, and your choice of theme | Your local machine |

**Agent sessions belong to the server, not to your window.** If you close the window, lose the network, or put the laptop to sleep, the sessions keep running. When you reconnect, from this machine or a different one, the sessions are listed and you can resume them. If the server itself goes away, you can still resume the conversation.

Kepler runs agent sign-in on the host. Claude Code, Codex, and Auggie all sign in to a remote target: Kepler starts the flow on the host, the sign-in page opens in your *local* browser, and Kepler saves the credential on the host. For Claude Code and Auggie, you paste back what the sign-in page gives you. Codex signs in with **ChatGPT (device code)**, which *works on any machine*, with an API key, or with **Import local Codex login**. See [Agent Integrations](/kepler/agent-integrations).

> **Note:** Remote windows use this app's interface. When the host runs a different version of Kepler, Kepler offers to update the server or this app. To show the host's own interface instead, turn off **Settings → Remote environments → Remote windows → Always use this app's interface**, which is on by default.

**Themes belong to this computer.** Every window lists and installs themes from this computer's themes folder and gallery, including a window on a remote machine. Every window opens in the theme you chose.
